title: Node Atlas + Heartbeat: Routing & Inventory Playbook
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc captures a pragmatic design for a lightweight cluster inventory (Node Atlas) and heartbeat protocol that drives routing policies in multi-region Redwood deployments. It focuses on: node identity and labels, GPU capability modeling, health signal aggregation, local vs global control-plane flows, and the impact on request routing (affinity, fallbacks, and capacity-aware scheduling).

Principles / constraints:
- Inventory must be eventually consistent across control-plane components but allow strong local reads for routing decisions (read path within region should not require global synchrony).
- Health signals should be low-bandwidth and resilient to transient noise; routing uses a smoothed health score rather than raw counters.
- GPU descriptors must be expressive enough for kernel-selection and fallback decisions (model quantization/compatibility).
- Keep per-node document small (< 2 KB) to allow efficient broadcast / caching.
- Support fast drains and soft-decommission for maintenance without global disruption.

High-level components:
- Node agent (on-host): emits heartbeat, local telemetry (temp, GPU utilization, GPU ECC), and registers node catalog entry at startup.
- Regional Node Registry: region-scoped store (etcd-backed or Dynamo-like) that accepts heartbeats, computes regional health indexes, and serves local routing queries.
- Global Inventory Index: sharded index for cross-region queries (capacity/availability); used for policy-level decisions (e.g., prefer region with spare NVMe-backed pools).
- Router / Scheduler: consumes regional registry + global index snapshots to make routing decisions; uses TTL-based caching.

Node Atlas schema (compact, field list):
- node_id (string): stable UUID
- short_name (string): human-friendly (rack-1-gpu-a)
- region (string)
- zone (string)
- instance_type (string)
- labels (list[string]): team, tenancy, isolation_tags, hw_pool
- gpu_vendor (string): nvidia/amd/others
- gpu_model (string): e.g., a100-80gb, h100-80gb, rtx6000
- gpu_count (string): e.g., "2"
- vram_gb (string): e.g., "80"
- vram_effective_gb (string): account for shared memory / OS reservations
- pci_gen (string)
- cuda_driver (string)
- container_runtime_hash (string): opaque image hash for runtime compatibility checks
- last_heartbeat_ts (string, iso8601)
- heartbeat_interval_s (string)
- health_score (string): 0..100 (see health scoring below)
- soft_drained (string): true|false
- routing_tags (list[string]): e.g., "low-latency", "high-throughput", "quant-safe"
- capacity_units (string): normalized unit for quick capacity math

Design notes on labels and routing_tags:
- labels are authoritative metadata used by inventory queries. routing_tags are derived (or manually set) tags used directly by the router; routing_tags should be sparse and curated to avoid combinatorial explosion.
- Example labels: ["gpu:a100","owner:dedicated-x","tier:dedicated"]
- Example routing_tags: ["llm-short-seq","batch-lower-priority","quantized-ok"]

Health signals & scoring (recommended):
1) Raw signals we collect (host-level and GPU):
   - host_cpu_pct (1m avg), gpu_util_pct (1m avg), memory_available_mb, gpu_temp_c, gpu_power_w, gpu_ecc_errors, disk_io_wait_ms, last_heartbeat_age_s, recent_restarts_count
2) Smoothing windows:
   - short (1m), mid (5m), long (1h) — router weights mid-window most heavily for transient resistance.
3) Scoring function (0-100): base=100, subtract penalties for thresholds crossed; apply decay for missed heartbeats. Apply caps so spike in one signal doesn't drop score catastrophically.
4) Health bins for routing: healthy (90-100), degraded (60-89), at-risk (30-59), offline (<30).

Routing policy examples using Node Atlas:
- Latency-affine: prefer nodes with region==request.region and health_score>=85 and routing_tags contains "low-latency". If none available, expand to cross-zone same-region low-latency nodes. If still none, fallback to regional degraded nodes with a cap on token rate.
- Cost-aware fallback: prefer quantized-ok nodes when model variant is quantized. If model requires FP16 and quantized-ok==false, fallback to lower-throughput but higher-precision nodes in another region only if latency < 300ms.
- Burst routing: allow bursting to Dedicated pool when regional free_capacity_units > threshold. Use short-lived leases to lock capacity_unit before request execution.

Control plane sync patterns:
- Local-first reads: Routers query regional registry cached snapshot (TTL 5s–30s depending on SLO).
- Delta push for global index: regions push compact diffs (node_id + small descriptor) to global index every 30s or on topology change. Global index is optimized for capacity search (e.g., find any region with N capacity units for model X).
- Fan-in for rare writes: configuration changes (soft_drained toggles, label updates) go through a regional write path and are then fan-out via a change log to subscribers.

Heartbeat protocol (practical):
- UDP or gRPC keepalive: choose gRPC (reliable, auth) with small protobuf payload. Heartbeat includes node_id, last_heartbeat_ts, rolling telemetry summary for short window, and a short signature.
- Back-pressure and batching: if agent has many small signals, batch summary every heartbeat_interval (default 10s). For high-cardinality telemetry (per-core metrics) export via separate telemetry pipeline; do not put heavy telemetry in heartbeat.
- Missing heartbeat handling: router treats heartbeat_age > 3x heartbeat_interval as degraded; > 6x => offline.

Capacity model and units:
- Introduce capacity_units normalized to model footprint: e.g., a single A100-80gb = 100 units, H100-80gb = 140 units, smaller GPUs proportional. Use model-specific token/sec estimates to convert to capacity_units for a given model.
- Node capacity_units = sum(gpu_count * per_gpu_unit * health_scale). health_scale derived from health_score.

Operational flows and runbooks (sketch):
- Node maintenance (soft drain): set soft_drained=true on node; control-plane rebalances new requests away within TTL window; existing requests continue; once drained, mark out_of_rotation and schedule safe reboot.
- Fast recovery (GPU ECC surge): if ECC errors spike, health_score moves to at-risk; auto-evacuate routing after N errors sustained for M minutes; generate Slack alert to #plat-ops with node_id and recent logs link.

Multi-region consistency tradeoffs: 
- We prioritize local routing speed over global freshness. A stale global index can cause suboptimal cross-region routing but won't break locality-first SLOs.
- For critical enterprise customers, allow "pinned" mode: their routing consults global index synchronously for strict placement constraints (higher latency but deterministic).

Data-plane security and auth:
- Node agent authenticates with short-lived mTLS certs issued by regional CA. Heartbeats are signed. Registries enforce digest checks for container_runtime_hash to prevent runtime divergence.

Telemetry and observability hooks:
- Expose metrics: heartbeat_age_histogram, region_free_capacity_units, nodes_in_degraded_bin, per-routing-policy_missrate
- Traces: when router falls back to cross-region, emit trace with decision tree and node_snapshot. Useful for postmortems and policy tuning.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we want a single health_score or multiple orthogonal ones (cpu_health, gpu_health, infra_health) so routing policies can pick which matters? (pros: more precise routing; cons: more complexity in scoring).
- Vectorizing capacity calculation for mixed-GPU nodes (shared vram among containers) — need test harness and realistic load traces.
- Decide on exact TTLs for regional cache vs router staleness budget. Start conservative: 10s TTL, revisit after canary.

Action items:
- Marcus: prototype capacity_units mapping script and synthetic load test by 2025-01-22.
- Elena: add schema v2 proto and a compact delta format for global index by 2025-01-10.
- Priya: instrument router to emit fallback traces and heatmap for 2-week canary.
- Aisha: draft rollout runbook for soft drains and GPU ECC event handling.

Appendix: quick example node atlas entry (one-line compact form):
node_id=ae12-... | region=us-west-2 | zone=us-west-2a | gpu=a100-80gb:2 | vram=160 | health=92 | last_hb=2024-11-15T18:22:31Z | tags=[low-latency,quantized-ok]

Slack refs: #infra-node-atlas, #plat-ops
Jira: PLAT-788 (global index), PLAT-812 (health scoring), PLAT-816 (heartbeat proto)

Notes: this is intentionally pragmatic — focus on a low-friction rollout (start regional-only, short TTLs), measure, iterate. Keep message formats compact; avoid heavy telemetry in heartbeat itself.
